q: Why must respiration occur continuously in every living cell, rather than only when the organism is active?
options: Cells keep large ATP reserves, but these must be topped up after each period of high activity such as exercise
ATP is used within seconds and can't be stored or shared between cells, so each cell must keep remaking it
Only muscle and liver cells actually need ATP; other cells respire mainly to get rid of excess glucose
ATP is made mainly in the liver and carried in the blood plasma to other cells, so the liver respires nonstop
explanation: Even at rest, cells need a constant ATP supply for active transport (e.g. Na+/K+ pumps), protein synthesis and other processes. ATP is unstable, present only in small amounts and not transported between cells, so every living cell – including plant root and leaf cells, day and night – must respire continuously to regenerate ATP from ADP + Pi.
